title: The clinical relevance of multiple sclerosis genetics: from susceptibility to disease severity and progression
title_zh: 多发性硬化症遗传学的临床意义：从易感性到疾病严重程度与进展
abstract: Large-scale genome-wide association studies have identified hundreds of multiple sclerosis risk loci, most of which implicate immune pathways and establish multiple sclerosis as a highly polygenic, immune-mediated disease. These findings help explain why immune-modifying therapies suppress relapses and new lesion formation. However, susceptibility genetics does not adequately explain disability accumulation, variation in disease course, or treatment response. Evidence from rare-variant studies, genetic studies of disease severity and disability progression, epigenetic analyses, gene-environment studies, and Epstein-Barr virus research is beginning to extend this genetic framework from susceptibility to disease expression. Still, the direct clinical relevance of this research remains constrained by modest individual-level predictive value, underpowered studies of genetic determinants of disease severity and disability progression, complex regulatory mechanisms linking variants to function, and restricted generalisability across populations. At present, multiple sclerosis genetics is most useful for interpreting mechanisms, prioritising therapeutic targets, supporting causal inference, informing biomarker discovery, and enriching research cohorts. Future clinical value will likely depend on integrating genetic architecture with longitudinal clinical, imaging, biomarker, and multi-omic data to identify the contexts in which prevention or treatment is most likely to succeed.
abstract_zh: 大规模全基因组关联研究已识别出数百个多发性硬化症风险位点，其中大多数涉及免疫通路，确立了多发性硬化症为一种高度多基因、免疫介导的疾病。这些发现有助于解释为何免疫调节疗法能抑制复发和新病灶形成。然而，易感性遗传学并不能充分解释残疾累积、疾病进程的差异或治疗反应。来自稀有变异研究、疾病严重程度与残疾进展的遗传学研究、表观遗传学分析、基因-环境研究以及EB病毒研究的证据，正开始将这一遗传框架从易感性扩展到疾病表达。尽管如此，该研究的直接临床相关性仍受限于个体预测价值有限、针对疾病严重程度和残疾进展的遗传决定因素研究样本量不足、将变异与功能联系起来的复杂调控机制以及跨人群的普适性受限。目前，多发性硬化症遗传学最有用的方面是解释机制、优先考虑治疗靶点、支持因果推断、指导生物标志物发现以及丰富研究队列。未来的临床价值可能取决于将遗传结构与纵向临床、影像、生物标志物和多组学数据整合，以识别预防或治疗最有可能成功的情境。
